title: How to Clean Inside Your Windshield (No Haze, No Streaks)
hook: You clean the inside of your windshield, and it looks worse than before. Smears, a greasy haze, and a blinding glare at sunset. The problem isn't you, it's the method. In seven steps, you'll learn the simple way to get the glass truly clear. It takes about ten minutes, costs almost nothing, and you will notice the difference immediately. Plus a fix for stubborn haze.
intro: The inside of a windshield gets a special kind of dirt. It's a thin oily film, caused by plastics and vinyl in the dashboard that release vapors in the heat, and by your own breath and fingers. A regular wipe just spreads that film around. The fix is a clean dry start, two cloths, and a very light touch of cleaner. Everything we'll use is cheap and safe for the car's interior. Before we start, remember never to clean the windshield while driving, and only do this with the car parked.
youNeedNarration: Here's what you need. Two clean, dry microfiber cloths, and a third if you can. An ammonia-free glass cleaner, or a half and half mix of distilled water and isopropyl alcohol. A small towel to protect the dashboard. And, if your hands can't reach the corners, a simple reach tool, such as a windshield wand, or a sponge on a stick. You may already have all of this at home.
heroImagePrompt: View through a spotless car windshield from the driver seat toward a sunny road, clean glass, dashboard in the foreground, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Park in the shade and prep
steps.narration: Step one. Park the car in the shade, with the engine off and the keys out of the ignition. Hot glass dries cleaner too fast and leaves streaks, so wait until the windshield is cool to the touch. Open the doors for ventilation, and lay a small towel over the dashboard to catch drips and protect the plastic. Remove any phone mounts, toll tags or dashcams you can, and if the cameras and sensors near the mirror are present, leave them alone, and don't spray them. Check that the wipers are lifted off the glass, so you don't have to clean around them. This one minute of preparation makes the rest much faster.
steps.mistake: Cleaning hot glass in direct sun
steps.imagePrompt: A parked car in the shade with the doors open and a towel laid on the dashboard, bright day, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Dust and wipe it dry first
steps.narration: Step two. Before you add any liquid, wipe the glass with a dry, clean microfiber cloth. This lifts the dust and loose grit, so you won't turn it into mud with the cleaner. Work in one direction, from top to bottom, and fold the cloth to a fresh side as it gets dirty. Pay attention to the corners and the area near the dashboard. If the cloth comes away with a grey, greasy smear, that is the film we are about to remove. Pay attention to the area along the top edge, because dust tends to collect there in thick lines.
steps.imagePrompt: A hand with a folded microfiber cloth wiping dust off the inside of a car windshield, bright light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Reach every corner
steps.narration: Step three. The hardest part is reaching the lower corners, where the glass meets the dashboard. Sit in the passenger seat to clean the driver side and vice versa, or move the seat back and lean over the wheel. A windshield wand, or a sponge-head tool, wrapped with a microfiber cloth, makes it easy. You can also fold a cloth over a flat spatula or a small ruler. Take your time, and don't force your arm into awkward positions. The better you reach, the better the result. Wrapping the cloth around the tool, and securing it with a rubber band, stops it from slipping off while you work. If the tool leaves lint, change the cloth.
steps.tip: Use a reach tool for the corners
steps.mistake: Straining to reach with your fingertips
steps.imagePrompt: A long-handled windshield cleaning wand with a microfiber pad reaching the lower corner of a car windshield, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Apply cleaner to the cloth
steps.narration: Step four. Lightly spray ammonia-free glass cleaner onto the microfiber cloth, not directly on the windshield, so no liquid runs down onto the dashboard and electronics. Ammonia can damage window tint and some dashboard plastics, so check the label. As an alternative, use a mix of equal parts distilled water and isopropyl alcohol. The cloth should be barely damp. Wipe in straight lines, from side to side, overlapping each pass a little, so you cover the whole surface. A little cleaner does more than a lot. Work in small sections so the cleaner never dries on the glass before you buff it away, and don't forget the top edge.
steps.mistake: Using ammonia cleaner on tinted glass
steps.imagePrompt: A spray bottle of glass cleaner spraying onto a folded microfiber cloth, bright car interior, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Buff with a dry cloth
steps.narration: Step five. Immediately follow with a second, completely dry microfiber cloth, while the glass is still slightly damp. This is the secret to no streaks. Buff in vertical strokes, from top to bottom, if you cleaned with horizontal strokes before, because streaks run in one direction, and a change of direction makes them easy to spot. Use light pressure and flip the cloth to a clean side regularly. A dirty cloth just redistributes the film, so switch cloths if it becomes damp. Take your time with the final pass. This is the stage that decides whether the glass looks perfect or just acceptable.
steps.imagePrompt: A hand buffing the inside of a car windshield with a dry microfiber cloth in vertical strokes, sun glare behind, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Check the glass at an angle
steps.narration: Step six. Now inspect your work. Look at the windshield from a few angles, because haze is easiest to see from a low angle or with the sun shining through. If you see streaks or a cloudy patch, repeat the damp and dry method on that area only. Check the lower edge and the corners again. Also clean the back of the rear-view mirror and the edge of the glass, where the black dots are. Then put the dashcam and phone mount back. Walk around and check from the passenger seat too, because the view from there is different, and reveals more.
steps.tip: Look through the glass toward the sun
steps.imagePrompt: The view through a spotless windshield with bright sunshine and no streaks, a road ahead, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Keep the haze from returning
steps.narration: Step seven. The film builds up again over time, but you can slow it down. Don't touch the glass with your fingers. Avoid smoking and vaping in the car. Clean the dashboard with a damp cloth too, because dust and vapors from dirty plastic end up on the glass. Avoid shiny dashboard sprays, which make a lot of haze. Open the windows occasionally to ventilate the car in summer. Repeat this cleaning every month or two, and the job will stay quick. A clean windshield is not only nicer, it's also safer, because glare at night and at sunrise is reduced.
steps.tip: Do it monthly, it takes ten minutes
steps.imagePrompt: A clean car dashboard with a matte finish and a microfiber cloth lying on it, bright light, photorealistic, no text

bonus.label: STILL STUCK?
bonus.title: Haze that keeps coming back
bonus.narration: Still hazy? Try a two-pass wash: first a cloth barely damp with distilled water and one drop of dish soap, which lifts oily film, then plain distilled water to remove the soap. If haze returns within days, the dashboard plastic is probably releasing vapor onto the glass.
bonus.imagePrompt: A hand holding a folded white microfiber cloth against the inside of a car windshield, a small glass bowl of clear water on the dashboard towel, sunlit hazy glass on one side and clear glass on the other, interior view from the passenger seat. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: CALL A PRO
bonus.title: When to call a glass shop
bonus.narration: Some windshield problems are not a cleaning job. A small chip can often be repaired if you act early, so cover it with clear tape to keep dirt out. After a replacement, a camera behind the mirror may need recalibrating.
bonus.tip: Tape a chip, then get it repaired early
bonus.imagePrompt: Close-up of a small star-shaped chip in a car windshield with a strip of clear tape over it, blurred road and trees visible through the glass, daylight. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: KEEP IT CLEAN
bonus.title: Keep the glass clear longer
bonus.narration: Keep your glass cloths in a zip bag in the glove box, so they stay clean. Wipe your wiper blades with a damp cloth now and then, because a dirty blade smears the glass. Replace the cabin air filter on the schedule in your manual, since a clogged one lets in more dust.
bonus.imagePrompt: A tidy car interior seen from the driver seat, a folded microfiber cloth resting on the passenger seat, a spotless windshield showing a bright street ahead, soft morning light. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

mistakesToAvoid.narration: Let's look at the mistakes that cause streaks. First, spraying cleaner directly onto the glass. It runs onto your dashboard, and it leaves too much liquid behind. Second, using a dirty or used cloth, or a paper towel, which leaves lint. And third, cleaning in the sun, on hot glass, where the liquid dries before you can wipe it. Do the job in the shade, use clean microfiber, and go lightly with the cleaner. It really is that simple. Keep a dedicated glass cloth, and wash it without fabric softener, which leaves a greasy film.
items: Spraying cleaner straight onto the glass
Using dirty cloths or paper towels
Cleaning hot glass in the sun

recap.narration: Let's recap. Park in the shade and prepare the car. Dust and wipe the glass dry first. Find a way to reach every corner. Apply a little cleaner to the cloth, not the glass. Buff with a second dry cloth. Check the glass at an angle. And keep the haze from coming back with a few good habits. Seven steps, about ten minutes, and a windshield you can't see at all. If haze comes back, use the two-pass wash, and know when a glass shop is needed.
items: Park in the shade and prep
Dust and wipe it dry first
Check the glass at an angle

outro: That's how you clean the inside of your windshield without haze or streaks. If your glass is crystal clear now, subscribe to WikiTube, because we publish a new how-to every single day. Tell us in the comments what you want us to clean next. See you tomorrow.

metadata.title: How to Clean Inside Your Windshield (No Haze, No Streaks)
metadata.description:
Streaky, hazy windshield that glares in the sun? In this step-by-step video you'll learn how to clean the inside of your windshield with no haze and no streaks. We cover why the inside film builds up, the right cloths, how to reach the corners, using cleaner on the cloth instead of the glass, buffing with a dry microfiber, and how to keep it clear. Simple, cheap, and safe for tinted windows.

You'll need: two clean microfiber cloths, ammonia-free glass cleaner, distilled water, a small towel, a reach tool or sponge.
